title: Set relations when a ticket is created or updated
description: Today a relation is added with a separate command: heist relation add SOURCE TARGET TYPE. Add flags to heist ticket create and heist ticket update so the links are written in the same call: --blocked-by A,B (each listed ticket blocks this one), --blocks A,B (this ticket blocks each listed one) and --relates A,B (relates_to, no effect on readiness). Tickets are named by key or id, separated by commas. Outside the happy path: an unknown ticket in any flag stops the command before anything is written, so no half-linked ticket is left behind; the same ticket in --blocked-by and --blocks is refused; on update a relation that already exists is skipped without an error; a blocks relation that would close a cycle is refused with the existing cycle message; with --format json the output stays the ticket only.
why: Only 9 relations exist among 42 tickets, because a relation needs a second command after ticket create and is easily left out. Readiness, heist next and the roadmap views only show what is linked.

acceptance.text: heist ticket create with --blocked-by, --blocks and --relates writes the relations in the same call
heist ticket update accepts the same flags
An unknown ticket key stops the command and no ticket and no relation is written
heist --help, heist guide and the README name the flags

outcome.summary: Both child tickets were done by a Haiku subagent from the tickets alone; reviewed by the planner: diff read, tests run.
